chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Abu Hamza, from Abu Baseer, who said:

He (peace be upon him) said: When something from the four determined Verses is recited and you hear it, then prostrate (Sajdah), and even if you are without ablution, and even if you are in a state of major impurity (Junub), and even if the woman is not praying (due to menstruation); and for the rest of the Quran, you have the choice therein: if you wish, you prostrate, and if you wish, you do not prostrate.

key_terms.الْعَزَائِمِ الْأَرْبَعِ: The four determined/mandatory verses of prostration
key_terms.جُنُباً: In a state of major impurity (post-sexual emission)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prostration during Quran recitation for those without ablution or in major impurity?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the distinct legal status of the four 'determined' verses (Al-A'raf 206, Ar-Ra'd 15, Al-Isra 109, and Al-Najm 62), where prostration is obligatory (wajib) even for those in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) or menstruation, unlike the remaining verses where it is optional (mandub). This ruling underscores the unique reverence accorded to these specific verses in Shia jurisprudence, prioritizing immediate submission to the Divine command over the prerequisite of wudu or ghusl.
